text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Parliament will start debates on amendments to the 1991 land law.

- The Agriculture Ministry plans to give private farmers coupons worth 1,400 billion lei to help them complete seasonal works. The Finance Ministry will have to decide on the value of each coupon, the paper said.
- Workers at Azochim SA chemical plant in Piatra Neamt threatened to block roads in the area to protest against lack of funds for new investments at the plant.
ADEVARUL
- The central bank will not intervene to influence the exchange rate of the local leu currency against the dollar, the paper said.
- Private farmers asked the government to support the sector with funds.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Electricity supplies were cut in some 500 localities where strong winds and hailstorms damaged the lines.

- NATO members are divided over the question of inviting Romania to join the Alliance in the first wave of enlargement, with most European members in favour of an early admission, despite a U.S. decision to support only Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, the newspaper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies voted to allow the restitution of up to 50 hectares of farmland. Under a 1991 land restitution law Romanians could get back up to 10 hectares of land confiscated by the ousted Communists. The law needs to clear the upper Senate house, too.

- Troubled private bank Dacia Felix will start reimbursing deposits of up to 20 million lei and interest, following a deal with U.S. investment fund American National Group which took over the bank's assets and debts.
ADEVARUL
- The justice minister sacked most of the staff in the country's General Penitentiary Division on grounds of corruption.

- Members of three county organisations of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) have resigned over the past two days to join reformists, led by former foreign minister Teodor Melescanu, who quit the party in protest at its conference last week.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The American Jewish Committe supports Romania's bid to get early NATO membership.
- A Tarom Airbus 310 on a flight to New Delhi, India, nearly collided with a Gulf Air Boeing 767 on Sunday, due to a miscalculation by Indian air traffic controllers.
- Meteorologists warn that heavy rainfalls, strong winds, thunderstorms and hail are expected over the coming days in southern and eastern Romania.
- Many Bucharest inhabitants mortgaged their houses with real estate companies against a monthly 10 percent interest rate, due to dropping living standards, the paper says.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
